sources.note: p.107: linguistic remains outside Gaul (Helvetian, Noric, Boic, Galatian) 'do not exhibit differences from Gaulish beyond the trivial' and are treated as Gaulish in the broad sense; the phonology section ('A thorny problem of Gaulish phonology') is about tau gallicum, no accent/stress section.

sources.citation: De Bernardo Stempel, Patrizia. 2006. From Ligury to Spain: Unaccented *yo > (y)e in Narbonensic votives ('gaulish' DEKANTEM), Hispanic coins ('iberian' -(sk)en) and some theonyms. Palaeohispanica 6: 45-58.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent/read the relevant passages: uses 'unaccented/unstressed *yo > e' as a Continental Celtic change; mentions the Norican ethnonym Laianci only as an onomastic parallel; no statement on where stress falls in Noric.

sources.note: Lists Noric among the marginally attested Continental Celtic varieties; the Proto-Celtic sound-change overview contains no statement on accent placement for Noric or Continental Celtic.

sources.citation: Eichner, Heiner, Janka Istenič & Milan Lovenjak. 1994. Ein römerzeitliches Keramikgefäß aus Ptuj (Pettau, Poetovio) in Slowenien mit Inschrift in unbekanntem Alphabet und epichorischer (vermutlich keltischer) Sprache. Arheološki vestnik 45: 131-142.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Eichner's linguistic part discusses letter forms and segmental values of the Ptuj inscription (e.g. whether zeta is an affricate /ts/ or a second sigma) and the interpretation Artebudz / Brogdui; no accent or stress statement (none possible from two names).

sources.note: The only full-length treatment of Continental Celtic stress position (reconstructed from syncope, gemination, vowel weakening in names); chapters IV-VI collect evidence across all Continental Celtic areas and would show whether Norican names (incl. Ptuj ARTEBUDZ/BROGDUI with apparent syncope) are used as stress-position evidence and what accent is inferred for East Celtic. Would be a comparative/second-order statement, the best obtainable for this Truemmersprache.
